content.text: I have the exact upstream diff for this change (apache/echarts PR #21113 by 100pah). Here is the plan.

input.summary: Add a new public option `visualMap.unboundedRange` (boolean, continuous type only, default `true`) that gates the "open interval" behaviour of `ContinuousModel.getValueState`. When `true`, a `range` whose low end touches `min` behaves as `[-Infinity, range[1]]` and whose high end touches `max` behaves as `[range[0], Infinity]`; when `false`, both ends are hard bounds so outliers outside `min`/`max` are always `outOfRange`. The opposite (non-touching) bound stays effective either way.
steps:
src/component/visualMap/ContinuousModel.ts — declare the new option in the `ContinousVisualMapOption` interface. Replace lines 47-52, currently:
```ts
    /**
     * selected range. In default case `range` is [min, max]
     * and can auto change along with modification of min max,
     * until user specified a range.
     */
    range?: number[]
```
with the updated `range` doc plus the new field (this sits between `calculable` at line 45 and the `hoverLink` doc block starting at line 53):
```ts
    /**
     * selected range. In default case `range` is `[min, max]`
     * and can auto change along with user interaction or action "selectDataRange",
     * until user specified a range.
     * @see unboundedRange for the special case when `range[0]` or `range[1]` touch `min` or `max`.
     */
    range?: number[]
    /**
     * Whether to treat the range as unbounded when `range` touches `min` or `max`.
     * - `true`:
     *   when `range[0]` <= `min`, the actual range becomes `[-Infinity, range[1]]`;
     *   when `range[1]` >= `max`, the actual range becomes `[range[0], Infinity]`.
     *   NOTE:
     *     - This provides a way to ensure all data can be considered in-range when `min`/`max`
     *       are not precisely known.
     *     - Default is `true` for backward compatibility.
     *     - Piecewise VisualMap does not need it, since it can define unbounded range in each piece,
     *       such as "< 12", ">= 300".
     * - `false`:
     *   Disable the unbounded range behavior.
     *   Use case: `min`/`max` reflect the normal data range, and some outlier data should always be
     *   treated as out of range.
     */
    unboundedRange?: boolean
```

src/component/visualMap/ContinuousModel.ts — do NOT add `unboundedRange` to `static defaultOption` (lines 278-310). Upstream deliberately keeps the default out of `defaultOption` and resolves it at read time via `retrieve2(..., true)`, so `chart.getOption().visualMap[0].unboundedRange` stays `undefined` unless the user sets it. The `range` clamping in `_resetRange` (lines 120-137, `range[0] = Math.max(range[0], dataExtent[0]); range[1] = Math.min(range[1], dataExtent[1]);`) is unchanged, which is why `range[0] <= dataExtent[0]` in practice means `range[0] === min`.

src/component/visualMap/ContinuousModel.ts line 207 — inside `findTargetDataIndices`, annotate the callback value param. Change `data.each(this.getDataDimensionIndex(data), function (value, dataIndex) {` to `data.each(this.getDataDimensionIndex(data), function (value: number, dataIndex) {`. Semantics of hoverLink target lookup (`range[0] <= value && value <= range[1]`, line 208) are intentionally NOT gated by `unboundedRange` — `ContinuousView._doHoverLinkToSeries` already substitutes `-Infinity`/`Infinity` into the passed range (ContinuousView.ts:800-801).

test/visualMap-on-data.html (currently 85 lines) — add a second manual test case. Insert `
` right after the existing `
` (line ~40), and append a second `

test/runTest/actions/__meta__.json — add `"visualMap-on-data": 1,` between `"visualMap-multi-continuous": 1,` and `"visualMap-selectMode": 2` (last three lines of the file; file ends with `}` and no trailing newline). Note: upstream's diff adds this entry without adding `test/runTest/actions/visualMap-on-data.json`; if the visual-regression runner requires the action file to exist, either record it or skip this step — it has no effect on unit tests or on the library build.

Optional but recommended verification: add a unit test under /workspace/test/ut/spec/component/visualMap/ (the only existing spec there is setOption.test.ts, which uses `createChart`/`getECModel` from '../../../core/utHelper'). Assert against `getECModel(chart).getComponent('visualMap', 0)` cast to ContinuousModel: with `{min: 0, max: 1000, range: [0, 500]}` and default/`unboundedRange: true`, `getValueState(-100) === 'inRange'` and `getValueState(600) === 'outOfRange'`; with `unboundedRange: false`, `getValueState(-100) === 'outOfRange'`; with `range: [500, 1000]` and `unboundedRange: true`, `getValueState(1200) === 'inRange'` while `getValueState(100) === 'outOfRange'`. Run with `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.js` (see /workspace/package.json scripts) and typecheck via the repo's `npm run checktype`/tsc task.
input.risks:
Base-state mismatch worth knowing: this workspace sits BEFORE apache/echarts PR #21104 (`requirements/visualmap-range-comparison.yaml`, also in this benchmark), so `ContinuousModel.getValueState` already contains the extent-aware open-interval logic — the requirement's claim that ranges "currently force both ends to behave as hard bounds" describes the post-#21104 tree, not this one. The upstream #21113 diff therefore will not apply cleanly; hand-apply the final form quoted above, which is a strict superset of both states. Consequence: with the default `unboundedRange: true` this change is a pure no-op for existing behaviour; only `unboundedRange: false` alters rendering. If #21104 is implemented in the same tree, it touches the identical function — #21113's version supersedes it and must win.

Other notes: `unboundedRange` is declared only on `ContinousVisualMapOption` (piecewise deliberately excluded — pieces already express open intervals); it reaches public typings automatically through `src/export/option.ts:58` (`ContinousVisualMapOption as ContinousVisualMapComponentOption`), so index.d.ts needs no edit. Because the default is resolved with `retrieve2` rather than declared in `defaultOption`, any test asserting the option round-trips through `chart.getOption()` will see `undefined`, not `true`. `getVisualMeta` (ContinuousModel.ts:223-276) and `getSelected` (165-179) are intentionally untouched, so the legend/gradient "singularity" stops still reflect the raw `range` regardless of the flag — a possible visual inconsistency upstream accepted.
